question: Related Questions Q. Regaring to the beard of imam-e-masjid 2132 views Q. Fajr Salah 2847 views Q. I am from India & presently working in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. I follow the Hanafi maslak. Sometimes due to work related travel I mis the jamat of Zohar salah. But I try to reach the masjid at the earliest to perform my Zohar salah. But sometime it happens that when I reach the masjid I find that Asar Jamat (as per Hambali timing) has started. But as per Hanafi salah timetable I still have time for our Zohar salah, as Asar time has not started as per Hanafi timetable. Now my question is what should I do? Do i read the Zohar salah first & then try to join the jamat of Asar which has already started may be the jamat may be over before I complete my Zohar salah. or I directly join the jamat for Asar salah & read my Zohar after that? I am very confused. But this happens only sometimes may be once in 3-4 months. 3561 views Q. How to offer Qaza-e-Umari Salah? 36871 views Q. answer: Prayers & Duties >> Salah (Prayer) Question ID: 40262 Country: India Title: Please clarify, are we allowed expressing our dua (in our own language/words) after Dua-e-Mathura and before salam of salah Question: (1) Please clarify, are we allowed expressing our dua (in our own language/words) after Dua-e-Mathura and before salam of salah? Whether the salah is fardh, sunnah, nawafil. Is this procedure correct and permissible? Answer ID: 40262 Posted on: Aug 30, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1149/739/H=1433) It is not lawful to supplicate in one’s own language before turning salam whether it is fardh, sunnah or nafl salah. However one can supplicate in one’s language after turning salam. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
